items.title: `writes_other` (a constraint of item A rewriting a type slot minted for item B) is not an invariant of the language — spike-49 measured 0 on kolt and R-b made it a standing pin, but a push into another module's use-inferred binding (`bag.push` from `a_spoil`, S1's third hazard) is exactly that write: the classes leg reads 49 constraint writes and kolt's drains 71 — the cross-item edge M110 S7's per-item records must carry
items.body: Measured with the id windows on (M110 S6): on kolt's served keystrokes the fixpoint's constraints write 0 slots outside their anchor's window (the spike's datum holds) while the prepped DRAINS (locals, assignments, std items — anchored in S6) write 71 (`writes_drain_other`): a name resolved in item A grounding a use-inferred binding minted for item B. On the edit-replay differential's classes package the constraints themselves write 49, all through `bag`/`a_spoil`'s cross-module push. So S6 pins `relocated_outside_anchor == 0` everywhere, `writes_other == 0` on the leaf package (no cross-module binding write) and REPORTS it elsewhere. For S7: a per-item record of item B is invalidated by A's write — the `entry_dirty_sources` of M19 at item grain — so the record must carry, per item, the slots other items' constraints and drains wrote (the counters already attribute each write to a window pair). Sizing: S for the edge table beside the records; the pin stays as written until S7 reads it.
